summary: Douglas Allen (b. 1941) works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt universities. He taught at Southern Illinois and Central Connecticut State, and was a long-time professor at the University of Maine from 1974.
Douglas Gildow specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University, where he studied under Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.
Douglas J. Penick (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1966 and trained under the traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

Douglas L. Berger is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Indology. He taught at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (attested 2007–2014) and holds posts at Leiden University as professor and Centre for Intercultural Philosophy director (attested 2026).

Douglas Ober works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under supervisor Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

Douglas Osto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Washington and a PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He joined Massey University in 2005, serving as Senior Lecturer and Programme Coordinator around 2007.

Douglas Q. Adams works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1968 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Idaho around 1972.

Douglas S. Duckworth (b. 1971) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and the University of Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), and served as an assistant professor at East Tennessee State University (~2008–2013).
Dragana Majhen works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's degree at the University of Manitoba under the supervision of Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his degrees at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, held posts there and with the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, and at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Dramdul works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2004–2012) and editor in chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013–2020).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin was a Buddhist figure who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Drolma is a scholar of Tibetology who completed an M. Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Keith Dowman, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak monasteries. He founded the International Nyingma Society and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Matthew T. Kapstein, and Alexander Berzin.
